business_problem: Matrix Renewables needed to onboard and monitor a rapidly growing portfolio of solar assets without the delays, data gaps, and scaling limits caused by decentralized monitoring across multiple SCADA systems.
solution_summary: Matrix Renewables standardized asset monitoring on IBM Maximo Renewables to create a centralized operating layer across its global solar portfolio. The platform ingests operational data from major SCADA providers such as GPM, AlsoEnergy, and Inaccess, plus seven tracker OEMs, using provider APIs rather than direct SCADA integrations. IBM optimized those API-based connections around query-frequency limits, concurrent-call restrictions, and timeout behavior so the company could maintain data quality and availability at scale. Within Maximo Renewables, AI and machine-learning analytics detect underperformance, uncover hidden inefficiencies, and support decisions that recover energy losses and improve ROI. The resulting data warehouse then feeds in-house BI reporting, real-time dashboards, alerts, and onboarding checks, giving asset managers a unified, scalable monitoring and reporting environment as Matrix continues international expansion.

solution_components.name: IBM Maximo Renewables
solution_components.role: Centralizes SCADA data, runs analytics on portfolio performance, and powers reporting and alerting for renewable assets.

data_flow: Operational data moves from SCADA provider APIs and tracker OEM systems into IBM Maximo Renewables, where analytics identify underperformance and energy-loss issues; curated portfolio data is then exposed through the Maximo-powered data warehouse to BI tools, dashboards, reports, and alerting workflows.
business_outcome: Matrix Renewables reduced reporting effort and downtime, improved production efficiency, increased transparency across operational and financial KPIs, and established a scalable monitoring platform for continued renewable-asset growth.
